mainTopic: The returnees' sin-offerings in עזרא, whether a communal חטאת can be brought after some of its owners have died, and whose view the ברייתא about a dead community member or judge follows.
overview: The גמרא finishes its point that a certain חטאת is not eaten. רבי יוסי then brings a similar case from ספר עזרא: the returnees from בבל brought twelve goats as a חטאת, yet the פסוק calls everything an עולה. The answer is that the goats were 'like an עולה' and were not eaten, because they were brought for the עבודה זרה of צדקיהו's time. The גמרא shows how each opinion in the משנה can explain twelve goats. It then asks how a חטאת could be brought when the sinners had died. רב פפא answers that a community never dies, and the גמרא searches for his source, finally showing that many elders of that generation were still alive. It also explains that a חטאת for deliberate sins was allowed only as a one-time ruling, a הוראת שעה. Finally, a ברייתא about a death in the community or in the בית דין leads to a debate between רב, רב יוסף and אביי over whether it follows רבי מאיר or רבי שמעון.

steps.title: This sin-offering is also not eaten
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the previous point: just as an עולה is not eaten, this חטאת is not eaten either.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too, the sin-offering is not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison it was making before this section: this particular חטאת is not eaten, just like an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the כהנים eat a חטאת. This line marks an exception: this one is burned and not eaten, just like an עולה. The next step brings a similar case.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering, brought to atone for a sin

phrases.english: so too, the sin-offering is not eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the comparison begun before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: This חטאת is not eaten; it is treated like an עולה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי quotes the returnees' offerings in עזרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי brings a similar case: the exiles who came back from captivity brought offerings, including twelve goats, and the פסוק says 'all was an עולה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way, רבי יוסי said: 'Those who came from the captivity, the exiles, offered burnt-offerings to the God of Israel, twelve bulls, etc., all was a burnt-offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי quotes a פסוק about the offerings brought by the Jews who returned from בבל. This sets up a puzzle the גמרא will raise next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'etc.' covers the rest of the פסוק, which mentions twelve goats as a חטאת. Yet the פסוק ends by calling everything an עולה. That is the problem the next step points out.

keyTerms.meaning: Similarly; a case just like it
A burnt-offering, completely burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: Similarly, Rabbi Yosei said:
"Those who came from the captivity, the exiles,
offered burnt-offerings to the God of Israel,
twelve bulls, etc.
phrases.notes: The part of the פסוק left out includes 'twelve goats as a חטאת.' That's the key detail.

phrases.english: all was a burnt-offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case of a חטאת treated like an עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק calls all the returnees' offerings, including the goats, an עולה.

steps.title: How can a sin-offering be a burnt-offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the plain reading: a חטאת cannot turn into an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think 'all was a burnt-offering'? Is it possible that a sin-offering is a burnt-offering?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the literal meaning of 'all was an עולה,' because the goats were clearly a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת and an עולה are two different kinds of קרבן with different laws. The פסוק itself calls the goats a חטאת, so it cannot mean they actually became an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (a way of rejecting a reading)

phrases.english: "All was a burnt-offering"? Can that enter your mind?
Is it possible that a sin-offering is a burnt-offering?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain meaning of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת cannot be an עולה; they are different types of offering.

steps.title: All was like a burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: Read the פסוק as 'all was LIKE an עולה': just as an עולה is not eaten, these goats were not eaten either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, all was like a burnt-offering: just as a burnt-offering is not eaten, so too this sin-offering is not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is making a comparison, not saying the goats changed type.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goats stayed a חטאת, but they were treated like an עולה in one way: nobody ate them, they were burned. This matches the type of חטאת brought for עבודה זרה, which is burned.
steps.whatToRemember: 'הכל עולה' means 'הכל כעולה': the goats were a חטאת that was not eaten, like an עולה.

phrases.english: Rather, all was like a burnt-offering:
just as a burnt-offering is not eaten,
so too the sin-offering is not eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rereading the פסוק as a comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The goats literally became an עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The goats stayed a חטאת but were not eaten, like an עולה.

steps.title: They were brought for idol worship in צדקיהו's time
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא with רבי יהודה says these offerings were for עבודה זרה; שמואל adds it was the עבודה זרה done in the days of צדקיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יהודה says they brought them for idol worship. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: for the idol worship they did in the days of צדקיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by showing these goats were brought for עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A communal חטאת for עבודה זרה is the kind that is burned, not eaten. So knowing they were brought for idol worship explains why they were 'like an עולה.' שמואל tells us which sin it was: the idol worship from before the destruction, in the days of צדקיהו.

keyTerms.meaning: The last king of יהודה before the first בית המקדש was destroyed

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
they brought them for idol worship.
And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁעָשׂוּ בִּימֵי צִדְקִיָּהוּ.
phrases.english: for the idol worship they did in the days of Tzidkiyahu.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer by naming the sin these goats atoned for.
steps.raayaObject: That these goats were a burned חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with רבי יהודה, and שמואל's addition.

steps.title: How does each opinion get twelve sin-offerings?
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון it is easy to explain twelve goats. But for רבי מאיר, who says only the בית דין brings, how can there be twelve?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for רבי יהודה: twelve tribes sinned and brought twelve goats. Or seven tribes sinned and the rest were pulled along. It also works for רבי שמעון: eleven tribes sinned and brought eleven goats, and the other one came from the בית דין. But for רבי מאיר, who says the בית דין brings and not the people, how do you find twelve?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the twelve goats against the three opinions in the משנה. Two opinions fit easily, and then it asks how רבי מאיר's opinion fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says each tribe brings its own offering, so twelve tribes means twelve goats. Even if only a majority (seven) sinned, the rest are pulled along. רבי שמעון also counts the בית דין, so eleven tribes plus the בית דין equals twelve. רבי מאיר says only one offering comes from the בית דין, so twelve is hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (opens a contrast with a problem)
You can find it; you can explain the case
Pulled along; included because the majority sinned

steps.confusionAlert: Here the goats are counted as separate offerings for separate groups. Do not think רבי מאיר disagrees about the פסוק; he only needs a different explanation for the number twelve.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rabbi Yehuda:

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ לְהָנֵי שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חַטָּאוֹת
phrases.english: you can find these twelve sin-offerings
in a case where twelve tribes sinned,
so they bring twelve goats.
Or also where seven tribes sinned,
and the rest of them are pulled along.
phrases.notes: Seven is a majority of the tribes, so the other five bring offerings along with them.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Shimon too, you can find it,
in a case where eleven tribes sinned,
so they bring eleven goats,
and the other one is from the court.
But according to Rabbi Meir, who says:
the court brings, and not the community,
how do you find twelve?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the twelve goats of the פסוק against each opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי מאיר's opinion can explain twelve communal sin-offerings.

steps.title: They sinned twelve separate times
steps.stepSummary: For רבי מאיר, the twelve goats came from twelve separate sins, one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case where they sinned, then sinned again, then sinned again, up to twelve times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the twelve goats were for twelve separate times of sinning, each needing its own offering from the בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows only one offering per sin. So the number twelve comes from repeating the sin twelve times, not from twelve tribes.

phrases.english: In a case where they sinned, and then sinned again,
and then sinned again, up to twelve times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how רבי מאיר gets twelve.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Twelve separate sins, each bringing one offering.

steps.title: But the sinners had already died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the people who sinned in צדקיהו's time were already dead, so how could an offering be brought for them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But those who sinned had died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new, bigger problem: the generation that sinned was gone by the time of the return from בבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת whose owners have died cannot be offered. Since the sinners from the days of צדקיהו were dead, it seems the returnees could not bring a חטאת for that sin. רב פפא answers this in the next step.

phrases.english: But those who sinned had died!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to שמואל's statement about צדקיהו and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the returnees brought offerings for the עבודה זרה of צדקיהו's time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת whose owners died cannot be offered, and the sinners were already dead.

steps.title: A community never dies, so its חטאת can still be offered
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the challenge: the rule that a חטאת whose owners died is left to die applies only to an individual, not to a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The tradition that a חטאת whose owners died must be left to die applies only to an individual. It does not apply to a community, because a community does not die.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 8 about how an offering could be brought for people who were already dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, if the owner of a חטאת dies, the animal is not offered. It is left to die. רב פפא limits this rule to a private person. A community, the צבור, keeps existing even when some of its members die, so its offering can still be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering whose owners have died
We have a tradition (a rule learned by הלכה למשה מסיני)

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying that a dead person's sin is ignored. He is saying that the community counts as the owner, and the community is still alive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one idea is the basis for the rest of the sugya, which tries to find where רב פפא learned it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי גְּמִירִי חַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ בְּמִיתָה –
phrases.english: When we have a tradition that a sin-offering whose owners died is left to die,
phrases.notes: "Left to die" means the animal is locked away until it dies and is never brought on the מזבח.

phrases.english: that applies to an individual,
but not to a community,
because there is no death for a community.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כִּי גְּמִירִי חַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ בְּמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 that the sinners of צדקיהו's time were dead.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a rule (individual versus community)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חטאת whose owners died can never be offered, so the goats of the returnees could not atone for the dead sinners.
steps.terutzMaskana: That rule is limited to an individual. A community's offering is still brought, because the community lives on.

steps.title: Where does רב פפא learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רב פפא's distinction between an individual and a community.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רב פפא know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב פפא's rule. This sets up the next few steps, where different sources are suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא stated a limit on a tradition, but he gave no proof. The גמרא wants to know what text or logic backs it up.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.english: From where does Rav Pappa know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule stated in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual source for the idea that a community's חטאת is offered even if some owners died.

steps.title: The פסוק about sons taking their fathers' place proves too much
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק 'instead of your fathers shall be your sons' and rejects it, because it would apply to individuals too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he learns it from the פסוק 'Instead of your fathers shall be your sons', then it should apply even to an individual!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible source and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק suggests that children stand in place of their parents. If that were the source, a son could bring his dead father's private חטאת. That goes against the known tradition. Since this פסוק cannot explain why only a community is different, it cannot be רב פפא's source.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introducing a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
"Instead of your fathers shall be your sons",
if so, it should apply even to an individual as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִדִּכְתִיב: תַּחַת אֲבוֹתֶיךָ יִהְיוּ בָנֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question of step 10 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It proves too much. It would let a son offer his dead father's private חטאת, which the tradition forbids.

steps.title: Proof from the ראש חודש goat paid for by the community
steps.stepSummary: The ראש חודש goat comes from the community fund, even though some of the donors have died since they gave. So a community's חטאת is offered even when some owners have died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא's proof is from the ראש חודש goat. The Torah says to bring it from the תרומת הלשכה, the Temple fund. But some of the people of ישראל who gave to that fund die. How can the rest bring it? So we learn that a community's חטאת is offered even if some of its owners died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a second source for רב פפא, this time from the goat brought on ראש חודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שעיר of ראש חודש is a חטאת bought with the half-shekels everyone gave in אדר. During the year, some of those donors surely die, yet the goat is still brought. That shows a community's חטאת is still offered even after some owners have died.

keyTerms.meaning: A precise inference drawn from a case
The goat חטאת brought on the New Moon
The Temple fund made from the half-shekels everyone gives

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa's inference
is from the goat of ראש חודש,
since the Merciful One said:
bring it from the Temple-chamber fund.
But some of ישראל die,
so how can those who remain bring it!
Rather, learn from it:
a sin-offering whose owners died is offered in the case of a community.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דּוּקְיָא דְּרַב פָּפָּא מִשָּׂעִיר דְּרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source was rejected, offers a new one.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that a community's חטאת is offered even if some owners died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The שעיר of ראש חודש, bought from community funds even though some donors die during the year.

steps.title: Maybe no one died there; here some surely died
steps.stepSummary: The ראש חודש proof is rejected. Perhaps none of the donors died, but in the time of the returnees, many of the sinners from צדקיהו's time had certainly died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? With the ראש חודש goat, maybe no one from the community died. But here, they certainly died!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ראש חודש goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the ראש חודש goat, it is possible that no donor has died yet, so the case proves nothing. With the returnees from בבל, so many years had passed that many of the sinners from צדקיהו's time had certainly died. The ראש חודש case cannot teach about a case where owners have certainly died.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
The goat of ראש חודש,
perhaps no one from the community died,
but here they certainly died!
phrases.notes: "Here" means the returnees from בבל, offering for the sin of צדקיהו's generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the שעיר of ראש חודש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case it is only possible that some donors died. In the returnees' case the sinners were certainly dead.

steps.title: Proof from the עגלה ערופה prayer, which atones even for those who left מצרים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק of עגלה ערופה, 'atone for Your people whom You redeemed', shows that this atonement reaches even those who left מצרים, who died long ago.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא's reason is from this פסוק: 'Atone for Your people ישראל whom You redeemed, ה׳.' This atonement is fit to atone even for those who left מצרים, since it says 'whom You redeemed'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third source for רב פפא, from the prayer said at the עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'whom You redeemed' point back to the people redeemed from מצרים. Those people died long ago, yet the atonement still covers them. This suggests that a community's atonement can reach its dead members.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken for an unsolved murder

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa's reason is from here,
as it is written:
"Atone for Your people ישראל whom You redeemed, ה׳",
phrases.notes: דברים 21:8, said by the elders at the עגלה ערופה.

phrases.english: this atonement is fit
to atone for those who left מצרים,
since it is written: "whom You redeemed".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ראש חודש proof was rejected, offers a new source.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that a community's atonement covers members who died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The עגלה ערופה פסוק, whose words 'whom You redeemed' include those who left מצרים.

steps.title: There the living are present; here was anyone alive?
steps.stepSummary: The עגלה ערופה works for the dead because living people are also being atoned for. But in the returnees' case, was anyone from צדקיהו's time still alive?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? There, everyone is present. Since the atonement works for the living, it also works for the dead. But here, were any of them alive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison to עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the עגלה ערופה, the atonement is mainly for the living people of the city, and the dead are covered along with them. In the returnees' case, if every sinner of צדקיהו's time had died, there would be no living people for the dead to be included with. So the comparison would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (one thing is true, so is the other)

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There, all of them are present,
since it atones for the living,
it also atones for the dead.
But here, were any of them alive?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from עגלה ערופה given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between עגלה ערופה and the returnees' offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עגלה ערופה covers the dead only as an add-on to the living. With the returnees there may have been no living sinners at all.

steps.title: Yes, some from the first בית המקדש's time were still alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that some people were still alive, as the פסוק in עזרא says that many old people who had seen the first בית המקדש wept.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is so, as it is written: 'And many of the כהנים, the לוים and the heads of the families...' who had seen the first Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that some people from צדקיהו's time were still alive among the returnees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in עזרא describes old people who had seen the first בית המקדש and cried when they saw the second one. So some of that generation were alive. Just like at the עגלה ערופה, the offering atoned for them, and the dead were covered together with them.
steps.whatToRemember: A community's חטאת is offered even if some owners have died, because the community never dies. The returnees' goats atoned for the living elders of צדקיהו's generation, and through them for the dead as well.

phrases.english: Yes, that is indeed so,
as it is written:
"And many of the priests and the Levites and the heads of the families, etc."
phrases.notes: עזרא 3:12. The rest of the פסוק says these elders had seen the first בית המקדש and wept.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, הָכִי נָמֵי, דִּכְתִיב: וְרַבִּים מֵהַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15, which supports the proof of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, some from צדקיהו's generation were still alive, as shown by the elders in עזרא who had seen the first בית המקדש.

steps.title: Maybe only a few old people were still alive
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the previous answer: perhaps the old people who wept were only a small group, not a large one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe they were only a few, and not many!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 16. Yes, some old people were alive, but maybe there were only a handful of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed that some people from צדקיהו's time were alive when the returnees brought their offerings. The challenge is that they may have been only a small group, while most of the people present were born later. If so, the living sinners might not be enough for the atonement to cover the dead along with them.

phrases.english: But perhaps they were few
phrases.notes: "They" means the old people who had seen the first בית המקדש and wept.

phrases.english: and they were not many!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא מוּעָטִין הֲווֹ וְלָא רַבִּים הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 16 by questioning how many survivors there were.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 16 that living people from צדקיהו's time were present.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small number of survivors may not count as the living community that the atonement needs.

steps.title: The weeping was as loud as the shouts of joy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from עזרא: the weeping could not be told apart from the shouts of joy, so the old people who wept must have been many.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it written: 'The people could not tell the sound of the joyful shout apart from the sound of the people's weeping, and the sound was heard far away'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק showing that the weeping was very loud. Loud weeping means many people were weeping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the crying of the old people was as loud as the joyful shouting of everyone else, there had to be a great many of them. So a large number of people from צדקיהו's time were still alive.

keyTerms.meaning: isn't it written? (introduces a פסוק as proof)

phrases.english: Isn't it written: "(And they did not recognize the sound)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: [And the people could not tell apart the sound] of the shout of joy
from the sound of the people's weeping [etc.]
and the sound was heard far away."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכְתִיב: וְאֵין הָעָם מַכִּירִים קוֹל תְּרוּעַת הַשִּׂמְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17 with a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a handful of old people survived from צדקיהו's time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The weeping was as loud as the joy, so the survivors were many.

steps.title: But they sinned on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the idol worship in צדקיהו's time was done on purpose, and a חטאת only atones for sins done by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they were deliberate sinners!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the whole case. How could the returnees bring a חטאת for sins that were done on purpose?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is brought only for a שוגג, a sin done by mistake. The people of צדקיהו's time worshipped idols knowingly, so they were מזידין. A חטאת should not work for them at all.

keyTerms.meaning: one who sins by mistake (the only kind of sin a חטאת atones for)

phrases.english: But they were deliberate sinners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of who was alive and attacks the case from a different direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the returnees' goats were a חטאת atoning for the sins of צדקיהו's time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת only atones for a שוגג, and these sins were done on purpose.

steps.title: It was a special one-time ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this was a הוראת שעה, a special ruling made only for that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a ruling for that moment only.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the normal rule was set aside just this once. The חטאת for deliberate sins was a special ruling for that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא agrees that normally a חטאת cannot atone for deliberate sins. This case was an exception made for the unusual situation of the return to ארץ ישראל. The normal rule stays the same.

keyTerms.meaning: a special one-time ruling for a specific moment, not a lasting law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not learn from this that a חטאת can atone for deliberate sins. The גמרא is saying this case was a one-time exception.

phrases.english: It was a ruling for that moment only.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A חטאת could never be brought for deliberate sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: Normally that is true, but here a special one-time ruling allowed it.

steps.title: The unusual numbers of rams and lambs prove it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the הוראת שעה answer. The returnees brought 96 rams and 77 lambs, numbers that match no Torah law, so they must have been brought under a special ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. If you don't say so, what do the '96 rams and 77 lambs' correspond to? Rather, it was a one-time ruling, and here too it was a one-time ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the same story. Some of the returnees' offerings clearly do not follow any regular law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers 96 and 77 do not match any offering commanded in the Torah, so they can only be explained as a הוראת שעה. Since those offerings were clearly a special ruling, the חטאת offerings brought at the same time were probably a special ruling too.

keyTerms.meaning: so too it is reasonable (introduces supporting logic)

steps.whatToRemember: The returnees' חטאת for the deliberate sins of צדקיהו's time was a הוראת שעה. The odd numbers of rams and lambs in the same פסוק show that special rulings were in force then.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for if you do not say so —
"ninety-six rams,
seventy-seven lambs" —
what do they correspond to?
Rather, it was a ruling for that moment only;
here too, it was a ruling for that moment only.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That the returnees' חטאת was a הוראת שעה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא 8:35, where the numbers of rams and lambs match no Torah law.

steps.title: A ברייתא: when someone dies before the offering is brought
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if one member of the community dies, the offering is still brought. If one member of the בית דין dies, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if one of the community died, they are obligated. If one of the בית דין died, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section with a ברייתא. It is about the case where the בית דין ruled wrongly, the community sinned, and someone died before the offering was brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the two kinds of death differently. If one person from the community dies, the offering is still brought. If one judge from the בית דין dies, no offering is brought. The גמרא will now ask whose opinion this follows.

keyTerms.meaning: obligated to bring the offering / exempt from it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If one of the community died, they are obligated;
phrases.notes: He means someone died after the sin but before the offering was brought.

phrases.english: if one of the court died, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֵת אֶחָד מִן הַצִּבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic about owners of a communal offering who died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A death in the community does not cancel the offering. A death in the בית דין does.

steps.title: Which תנא taught this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the ברייתא follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks which תנא holds the view in this ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the פרק there is a מחלוקת about who brings the offering: the בית דין, the community, or both. The answer will explain why the ברייתא treats the two deaths differently.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא? (whose opinion is this?)

phrases.english: Who is the תנא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view about who brings the offering fits the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב: it follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב says the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who holds that only the בית דין brings the offering. A dead member of the community changes nothing. A dead judge makes it a partners' חטאת where one partner died, so it is not brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רבי זירא, in the name of רב ירמיה, in the name of רב: it is רבי מאיר, who says the בית דין brings the offering and not the community. So if one of the community died, they are obligated, because the whole בית דין is still there. If one of the בית דין died, they are exempt, because it is a חטאת where one of the partners died, and that is why they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. He then explains both halves of the ruling based on that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, the owners of the offering are only the judges. A death in the community does not touch the owners, since the whole בית דין is still alive. When a judge dies, one of the owners has died, and a חטאת whose owner died is not offered. That is why they are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: since the entire court is still alive
a חטאת whose owner died; it is not offered

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said that Rabbi Zeira said
that Rav Yirmeya said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Meir, who says:
The court brings the offering, and not the community.

phrases.aramaic: הִלְכָּךְ מֵת אֶחָד מִן הַצִּבּוּר – חַיָּיבִין,
phrases.english: Therefore, if one of the community died, they are obligated,
since the entire court is still alive.
If one of the court died, they are exempt,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא לַהּ חַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּת אֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּתָּפִין,
phrases.english: since it is a sin-offering where one of the partners died,
phrases.notes: The judges are like co-owners of the חטאת, so when one dies it counts as an owner dying.

phrases.english: and because of that they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַב, רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי מאיר: only the בית דין owns the offering, so only a judge's death cancels it.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it could also fit רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רב: the ברייתא could also follow רבי שמעון, who says the בית דין and the community bring it together. The community never dies, but a judge's death still makes it a partners' חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Let us explain it according to רבי שמעון, who says the בית דין brings it together with the community. If one of the community died, they are obligated, because a community does not die. If one of the בית דין died, they are exempt, as we said, because it is a partners' חטאת!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף argues that רב had no need to pin the ברייתא on רבי מאיר alone. He shows that רבי שמעון's view gives the same results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון the community is also an owner. Still, a community as a whole is never considered dead, so one person dying does not matter. The judges, though, are a small set of partners, so a judge's death still cancels the offering. Both halves of the ברייתא work for רבי שמעון too.

keyTerms.meaning: he objected to it (introduces a strong challenge)
and let us explain it as following
a community does not die (as a whole it always continues)
the court together with the community

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected to this:
Let us explain it according to Rabbi Shimon,
who says: the court brings it together with the community.
If one of the community died, they are obligated,
since a community does not die.
If one of the court died, they are exempt,
as we said, because it is a sin-offering of partners!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: וְנוֹקְמַהּ כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's choice of רבי מאיר in Step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that the ברייתא must follow רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון's view explains both halves of the ברייתא equally well, so there is no reason to say it follows only רבי מאיר.

steps.title: אביי: רבי שמעון holds a partners' sin-offering is not left to die
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף. According to רבי שמעון, a חטאת שותפין is not left to die, so the ברייתא's ruling cannot fit רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: We have heard that רבי שמעון says a sin-offering owned by partners is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's suggestion that the ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון. The proof for his claim comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף explained the ברייתא through רבי שמעון by saying a judge's death turns the offering into a partners' חטאת where one partner died. אביי says רבי שמעון does not leave a partners' חטאת to die at all. If that is true, a judge's death should not exempt them, so the ברייתא must follow רבי מאיר, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering owned by several partners together
We have heard about him (we know his opinion)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, who just challenged רב.

phrases.english: We have heard of Rabbi Shimon that he says:
A partners' sin-offering is not left to die,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's challenge in Step 25 and so defends רב's reading in Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון does not leave a partners' חטאת to die, so the death of a judge could not exempt them under his view.

steps.title: Proof from the lost bull and goat of יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if the יום הכפורים bull and goat were lost and replaced, רבי יהודה says all are left to die. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say they graze, because a communal חטאת is not left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If the bull and goat of יום הכפורים were lost and others were set aside in their place, all of them are left to die, says רבי יהודה. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: They graze, because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the ברייתא that proves his claim about רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bull of יום הכפורים belongs to all the כהנים together, so it is a partners' offering. Even so, רבי שמעון does not let it die. It only grazes. אביי concludes that for רבי שמעון a partners' חטאת is not left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull and goat brought as sin-offerings on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: פַּר וְשָׂעִיר שֶׁל יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֶׁאָבְדוּ,
phrases.english: The bull and goat of Yom Kippur that were lost,
and he set aside others in their place,
they shall all die; these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
They shall graze,
phrases.notes: They graze until they get a blemish. They are not left to die.

phrases.english: because a communal sin-offering is not left to die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for אביי's claim in Step 26
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון holds a partners' חטאת is not left to die
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the lost bull and goat of יום הכפורים, where רבי שמעון rules they graze

steps.title: רב יוסף: priests are different because they are called a congregation
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that כהנים are a special case. The Torah calls them a קהל, so their bull is a communal offering, not an ordinary partners' offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: You bring a proof from priests? Priests are different, because they are called a congregation, as it is written: 'For the priests and for all the people of the congregation he shall atone.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes aside אביי's proof. He says the bull of the כהנים does not tell us how רבי שמעון treats an ordinary partners' חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק counts the כהנים as their own קהל. Their bull therefore falls under the rule that a communal חטאת is not left to die. A regular group of partners, like the judges, is not a קהל, so רבי שמעון could still let their offering die. That means רב יוסף's challenge against רב still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the כהנים count as a קהל, so their bull follows the rule of a communal חטאת. This does not prove that an ordinary partners' חטאת escapes death.
steps.whyThisMatters: Once אביי's proof is rejected, the ברייתא can still follow רבי שמעון, as רב יוסף claimed.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
You speak of priests?
Priests are different, for they are called a congregation,
as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל הַכֹּהֲנִים וְעַל כׇּל עַם הַקָּהָל יְכַפֵּר״.
phrases.english: "For the priests and for all the people of the congregation he shall atone."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: כֹּהֲנִים קָא אָמְרַתְּ? שָׁאנֵי כֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof from Step 27, so רב יוסף's challenge from Step 25 stands
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the כהנים are a קהל, unlike ordinary partners
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יום הכפורים bull is an ordinary partners' חטאת, so רבי שמעון never lets a partners' חטאת die
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהנים' bull counts as a communal חטאת because the Torah calls the כהנים a קהל. An ordinary partners' חטאת may still be left to die according to רבי שמעון.
